"You ate the last of the pickles," Marta said.

"I didn't."

"I watched you."

"You watched me eat a pickle. That was Tuesday. This is a different pickle situation entirely."

Leo set his fork down with the ceremony of a man surrendering a sword. "There was one pickle left in the jar this morning. Now there are zero pickles. You had a meeting until eleven. Do the math."

"The math." Marta opened the fridge and stared into it as if the jar might confess. "The math is that you bought those pickles with my grocery card."

"The math is that your grocery card is linked to my account, which is a separate indictment."

"Fine." She took out the eggs instead. "I'm making an omelet and you're not having any."

"You made that threat last week and then felt bad and shared."

"I felt bad once. I'm capable of growth." She cracked an egg one-handed, the way their mother used to, and held his stare the whole time, and he laughed first, which meant she won, which meant he got half the omelet after all.
